data.name: Naomiya
data.gender_notes: Naomiya is used as a unisex name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: In Hebrew, Naomiya means 'my delight' or 'my comfort'. This name has a rich history in the Bible, with the most famous bearer being the matriarch Naomi from the Book of Ruth. After suffering great loss, Naomi was comforted by her daughter-in-law Ruth, who remained loyal and committed to her family despite adversity. Through Ruth's unwavering love and dedication, Naomi was blessed with a new child, Obed, who became the ancestor of King David and the Messiah Jesus.
data.spiritual_meaning: Offering comfort and hope during difficult times, Naomiya is a name rooted in love, loyalty, and unwavering commitment.
data.etymology: Naomiya belongs to the Biblical linguistic tradition and is used in Christian naming. Its recorded meaning is “Comforted or delightful.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Naomiya total 6, giving a life-path number of 6. Number 6 is linked with Venus and with the qualities of responsibility, care and community.

in_hebrew.name: נאומיה
in_hebrew.meaning: נעימותיי, הנעימות של אלוהים, תענוג אלוהי
in_hebrew.long_meaning: נאומיה הוא שם עברי שפירושו 'נעימותיי' או 'תענוג אלוהי'. הוא מורכב משתי מילים: 'נעם' שפירושו נעימות או תענוג, ו'יה' שפירושו אלוהים. השם נאומיה הוא שם נדיר בישראל ובעולם היהודי, אך הוא מופיע בתנ'ך בספר רות, שם נאומיה היא אמה של רות, אשתו של מאחלון ודוד, וסבתא רבת של דוד המלך.

in_greek.name: Ναομία
in_greek.long_meaning: Το όνομα Ναομία είναι η ελληνική μορφή του εβραϊκού ονόματος נאומיה (Na'omiyah), που σημαίνει 'Χαρά του Θεού' ή 'Προσάρεμα Θεού'. Στην Καινή Διαθήκη, δεν αναφέρεται συγκεκριμένα το όνομα Ναομία, αλλά η Ναομία της Παλαιάς Διαθήκης αναφέρεται ως παράδειγμα γυναικός με αρετή και πίστη.

in_latin.name: Naomiya
in_latin.long_meaning: Nomen Naomiya origine hebraicum est, quod interpretatur 'Delectatio Dei' vel 'Gaudium Domini'. In traditione christiana, nomen Naomiya significat laetitiam et delectationem quae provenit ex Deo. In Ecclesia primitiva, nomen hoc non erat commune, sed in traditione hebraica et christiana, habet profundam significationem spiritualem.

in_english.name: Naomiya
in_english.meaning: Pleasure of God, Delight of the Lord
in_english.long_meaning: The name Naomiya originates from the Hebrew name נאומיה (Na'omiyah), meaning 'Pleasure of God' or 'Delight of the Lord'. It is derived from two Hebrew words: 'na'om' (נעם), meaning pleasantness or delight, and 'yah' (יה), referring to God. Although not directly mentioned in the New Testament, the name Naomiya reflects a deep spiritual significance in Christian tradition, symbolizing the joy and pleasure that comes from God. Historically, Naomiya was the name of Naomi, the mother-in-law of Ruth in the Old Testament, showcasing her faith and loyalty.

data.cultural_impact: Naomiya is a beautiful and meaningful name with roots in the rich Jewish traditions of the Bible. This name is a reminder of the importance of family, loyalty, and perseverance in the face of adversity.
data.spiritual_significance: Naomiya holds deep spiritual significance as it is a reminder that even in the darkest times, God is always present and offers comfort and consolation. The name carries a sense of hope and healing, as demonstrated by the story of Naomi in the Book of Ruth. Overall, Naomiya is a powerful and inspiring name that represents the enduring power of hope, love, and faith in God.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Naomiya, derived from the Hebrew name Naomi, means "pleasantness" or "comfort" in God. It is a reminder to seek solace and joy in the Lord during times of sorrow and hardship.

biblical_reference.note: Naomi's story in the book of Ruth exemplifies faith, loyalty, and the providence of God.

historical_references.reference: According to Jewish legend, Naomiya was a woman of Moab who took in her widowed daughters-in-law Orpah and Ruth when they were left destitute. Naomi urged them to return to their homeland and remarry. Orpah obeyed, but Ruth remained loyal and accompanied Naomi back to Bethlehem. Their reunion with Naomi's husband led to the marriage of Boaz and Ruth, and the birth of Obed, the grandfather of King David.

In Christian tradition, Naomiya is venerated as a saint and is the patroness of widows and those who have lost their families. The Roman Catholic feast day of Saint Naomiya is celebrated on December 27.
